note: Adversarial toy routing network (#73): a §2-conformant edge_attributes FeatureCollection used to harden the Phase-3 algorithms against real-network pathology (disconnected islands + one-way-only corridors) that the Porto extract will have but the hand-built toy_network.geojson does not. Two deliberate pathologies: (1) DISCONNECTED COMPONENT — nodes 4,5 and edge_id 4 (7100004:0:F) form an island with NO edge to/from the main component {0,1,2,3}, so an OD pair across the gap (e.g. node 0 -> node 4) is genuinely unreachable. (2) ONE-WAY TRAP — edge_id 3 (7100003:0:F, node 2 -> node 3) is one-way only: there is NO reverse row (no 7100003:0:R), so node 3 is a directed sink reachable forward from node 2 but with no edge leading back out. Routing the forbidden direction (node 3 -> node 2, or node 3 -> anywhere) must return a clean no-route, never traverse edge 3 backward. The main component also carries one genuine two-way street (7100002 F/R pair, node 1 <-> node 2) so 'no reverse edge' is a property of the trap specifically, not of every edge. All values computed at capacity_scale=1.0 via the §2 derivation rules exactly (capacity_vph = lanes x 1800 x class_factor; freeflow_time_s = length_m / (maxspeed_kmh / 3.6)). Region: NYC-ish, lon [-73.99..-73.9274], lat [40.73..40.7816]; the island sits ~7 km NE of the main component so NearestNode cannot accidentally bridge the gap. Coordinate deltas are sized so each edge's great-circle chord between its endpoints is strictly LESS than its declared length_m (a real OSM geodesic length_m is always >= the straight-line chord), keeping the fixture physically plausible and hardening against toy<->Porto drift. segment_ids are fresh 71000xx way ids (no overlap with toy_network.geojson or the congestion fixture) so the two fixtures never collide. See README.md.

features.note: MAIN COMPONENT entry: one-way residential node0(origin)->node1. defaults lanes=1, maxspeed=30. capacity=1*1800*0.5=900; freeflow=300/(30/3.6)=36.0.

TWO-WAY secondary, FORWARD half of the F/R pair node1->node2. Proves 'no reverse edge' is a property of the one-way TRAP specifically, not of every edge in the fixture. defaults lanes=2, maxspeed=50. capacity=2*1800*0.7=2520; freeflow=500/(50/3.6)=36.0.

TWO-WAY secondary, REVERSE half of the F/R pair node2->node1. Same way+seq as edge 1, dir=R: source_node/target_node swapped AND LineString coordinates reversed (source-first/target-last preserved per direction). Same split-default lanes_effective=2 and derived values.

ONE-WAY TRAP: a single directed row node2->node3 with NO reverse partner (there is no 7100003:0:R). node3 is therefore a directed sink — reachable FORWARD from node2 (node0->node1->node2->node3 is a valid path) but with no out-edge, so routing FROM node3 (e.g. node3->node2) must return a clean no-route and MUST NOT traverse this edge backward. defaults lanes=2, maxspeed=60. capacity=2*1800*0.8=2880; freeflow=600/(60/3.6)=36.0.

DISCONNECTED COMPONENT: a one-way tertiary node4->node5 on an island ~7 km NE of the main component, with NO edge connecting it to nodes {0,1,2,3}. An OD pair from the main component to this island (e.g. node0->node4) is genuinely unreachable; routing it must yield a defined no-route result (no panic/NaN/divide-by-zero). The ~7 km gap keeps NearestNode from accidentally snapping a main-component coordinate onto the island. defaults lanes=1, maxspeed=40. capacity=1*1800*0.6=1080; freeflow=400/(40/3.6)=36.0.
